newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Stability, growth are Yugo 97 economic goals - paper.
newsitem.headline: Stability, growth are Yugo 97 economic goals - paper.

text.p: BELGRADE, Nov 26 (Retuer) - Yugoslavia's top economic policy priorities for 1997 are price and currency stability, increasing production and exports and restructuring the economy, Belgrade daily Politika said on Tuesday.

Yugoslavia expected a 13 percent rise in gross domestic product and at least a 37 percent rise in exports while public spending should be reduced to 47.5 percent of GDP in 1997, the daily quoted Serbia's Prime Minister Mirko Marjanovic as saying.
Budget and public spending in Serbia will account for 35.3 percent of the republic's gross domestic product, he said.
The objectives, which remained the same as in the past two years, had been worked out between the federal and the two republics' governments as well as with the central bank, the paper said.
It also said the governments would insist on financial and budget discipline at all levels, especially in the public sector. -- Gordana Kukic, Belgrade Newsroom ++381 11 222 4254
